title: First friends in a new place
description: Starting again somewhere new is lonely before it is anything else — and that first stretch is not the verdict.

body.heading: Everyone is performing a little
paragraphs: In the first weeks of a new school, job, or town, nearly everyone is slightly acting: braver, funnier, more settled than they feel. Knowing this helps twice — you stop comparing your insides to their outsides, and you forgive your own performance as well.
The people who look instantly at home are often the most practised actors, not the most settled hearts.

body.heading: Anchor to one or two people
paragraphs: You do not need a crowd; you need one person whose name you know and one place where you are expected. A single lunch companion and a single weekly activity can carry you through the whole first season.
Kindness is a good compass here. Gravitate to the people who are decent to everyone, not only to the impressive. They are building the same kind of shelter you are.

body.heading: Keep the home fires lit
paragraphs: Old friends by message, family by call — these are not a failure to move on. They are the base camp that makes exploring the new place possible. New roots grow better in soil that is already warm.
And one day, sooner than it feels possible, you will give directions to a newcomer and realise the place has quietly become yours.

takeaway: Find one person and one regular place, keep old ties warm, and let time do its slow work.
